The square of the imaginary unit i is −1.why: The defining property of the imaginary unit, stated thousands of times and in the first lines of its Wikipedia article.

sources.quote: The imaginary unit, usually denoted by i, is a mathematical constant that is a solution to the quadratic equation x² = −1, which is not solved by any real number.
sources.note: The unit is defined as a solution of x² = −1.

sources.quote: The number −1 has two distinct complex square roots: i and its additive inverse −i.

sources.query: i is the square root of -1

The square of the imaginary unit i is a.why: The square of i is stated as −1, and −1 is known to be negative; no text says that the square of the imaginary unit is 'a negative number', since the value is always written out.

notes: ABox contraction paired with mathematics-replace-0013: removes 'The square of the imaginary unit i is −1' (has_square, functional). Mathematics has no worlds. Related asks about the cube of i, a different fact than the edit (the standard value is -i, stated in the article's table of powers): the cube is the square times i, so it depends on the edit. Derived: the cardinality question asks another candidate value, 1, and two compositions through the removed fact by description (is the square of i an integer; is it a negative number). Caveat: i² = −1 is the definition of the imaginary unit, so it is unclear what a contracted model should still know about i.
